repos.brief:
**What it does:** An open-source Chinese-authored book on AI Agent engineering—covering LLM context design, tool use, RAG, multi-agent systems, MCP, and reinforcement learning—with 92 runnable code experiments across 10 chapters, available as PDF/EPUB in 8 languages.

**Why now:** It gained 13,210 stars this week alone, signaling a surge in developer demand for structured, ground-up Agent engineering knowledge as context engineering emerges as a distinct discipline.

**Build with it:** Use the 70+ standalone experiments as scaffolding to prototype agents with memory, tool-calling pipelines, or multi-agent coordination—then reference the chapter on context engineering to tune what actually goes into your LLM's context window.

**What it does:** World Monitor is an open-source TypeScript dashboard that aggregates real-time news, geopolitical events, and infrastructure data into a single situational awareness interface, with an MCP server for AI agent integration and SDKs across npm, PyPI, RubyGems, and Go.

**Why now:** The project gained 13,065 GitHub stars this week alone, signaling rapid community adoption and likely a surge in contributors, issues, and API surface changes worth tracking if you're building on top of it.

**Build with it:** Wire the MCP server into a Claude or GPT-4 agent to trigger automated alerts when specific geopolitical conditions are met, or use the Python SDK to feed live event streams into a risk-scoring model for supply chain or financial exposure analysis.

**What it does:** OmniRoute is an open-source TypeScript gateway that routes requests across 290+ AI providers (90+ free tiers) through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with quota-aware auto-fallback and RTK+Caveman prompt compression that cuts token usage by 15–95%.

**Why now:** The repo gained nearly 11,000 stars this week, signaling rapid community adoption, and its free-tier aggregation (~1.53B tokens/month from 43 provider pools) makes it immediately practical as AI API costs and rate limits become a daily friction point for builders.

**Build with it:** Drop OmniRoute in front of any tool that speaks the OpenAI API—Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Copilot—and get seamless failover across free-tier providers without changing client code; then layer on the MCP/A2A support to wire it into multi-agent pipelines without hitting a single provider's quota wall.

**What it does:** OpenSEO is an open-source TypeScript SEO suite covering keyword research, rank tracking, backlink analysis, and site audits, built around a pay-as-you-go DataForSEO API key rather than a fixed subscription.

**Why now:** The repo gained nearly 3,000 stars this week, signaling strong breakout traction, and its MCP server integration makes it immediately usable inside Claude Code and other AI agent workflows that are hitting mainstream adoption right now.

**Build with it:** Self-host via Docker, plug in your DataForSEO key, and wire the MCP server into your AI agent to automate SEO audits, surface competitor keyword gaps, or build a white-label SEO tool for clients with custom Agent Skills.

**What it does:** Awesome Claude Skills is a curated collection of 1,000+ reusable instruction packages ("skills") that extend Claude and other coding agents like Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI with structured, domain-specific behaviors—backed by Composio's MCP Gateway for authenticated access to real-world app integrations.

**Why now:** The repo gained nearly 6,000 stars this week, signaling a surge in developer interest around Claude Code workflows and agent-to-app automation as teams move from chatbot experiments to production agent pipelines.

**Build with it:** Drop a skill folder into your Claude Code setup to give your agent repeatable, version-controlled behaviors—then wire it to Composio's MCP endpoint to let it actually send Slack messages, file GitHub issues, or trigger workflows across 1,000+ apps without writing custom auth code.

**What it does:** RuView uses ESP32 sensors (~$9/node) to capture WiFi Channel State Information and translate radio disturbances into real-time spatial data — presence, breathing rate, heart rate, fall detection, and sleep staging — through walls, with no cameras or wearables.

**Why now:** The repo spiked 5,495 stars this week, and it ships native integrations for Home Assistant, Apple Home, Matter, Google Home, and Alexa out of the box, making it immediately deployable into the smart home ecosystems most builders are already targeting.

**Build with it:** Wire an ESP32 mesh into an existing Home Assistant install with a single `--mqtt` flag and start publishing the 21 pre-built sensor entities — or extend the spiking neural network layer to add custom activity classifiers trained on your own environment in under 30 seconds.

**What it does:** jcode is a Rust-based CLI coding agent that runs AI models (Claude, OpenAI, and others) as a terminal TUI, using as little as 27.8 MB PSS RAM per session compared to Claude Code's 386.6 MB.

**Why now:** It gained 2,438 stars this week, signaling rapid community adoption at the exact moment developers are hitting RAM ceilings running multiple parallel AI coding sessions in CI pipelines and local dev environments.

**Build with it:** Use jcode as the backbone for a multi-agent orchestration system where dozens of concurrent coding sessions run on a single modest machine, or embed it into a cloud IDE product where per-user resource costs directly determine your margin.

**What it does:** ego lite is a macOS browser that gives AI agents like Claude Code and Codex their own isolated "Spaces" to run browser automation tasks using your existing logins and cookies, without touching your personal tabs.

**Why now:** The project gained 4,596 stars this week, signaling strong builder interest at the moment when agentic coding tools like Codex and Claude Code are being adopted for real workflows that require authenticated web access.

**Build with it:** Install the `ego-browser` skill via `npx skills add citrolabs/ego-lite` and wire it into a Claude Code or Codex agent to automate tasks like form submissions, dashboard scraping, or social actions against sites where you're already logged in—no credential management required.

**What it does:** opencodex is a local proxy that intercepts OpenAI Codex CLI/App/SDK and Claude Code API calls and reroutes them to any LLM provider — Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama, OpenRouter — by translating the Responses API into each provider's native format, including streaming, tool calls, and reasoning tokens.

**Why now:** It spiked 4,400+ stars this week, likely riding the wave of developers frustrated by Codex and Claude Code's locked provider models and seeking cost or capability alternatives — particularly as GPT-5 and Claude 4 pricing pressure pushes teams toward DeepSeek and Gemini.

**Build with it:** Point your existing Codex CLI or Claude Code workflow at `localhost:10100`, swap in a cheaper or more capable model without changing a line of application code, and build multi-agent pipelines where Claude Desktop and Grok Build call different subagent models across provider boundaries.

**What it does:** `code-review-graph` builds a persistent structural map of your codebase using Tree-sitter, then exposes it via MCP so AI coding tools pull only the relevant context instead of re-reading entire repos on every review.

**Why now:** The project gained 4,245 stars this week, signaling strong developer appetite for token-efficient AI workflows as teams hit real cost and latency walls with large-repo code review.

**Build with it:** Wire it into your Claude Code or Cursor setup to slash context overhead on PR reviews, or use the MCP server as a foundation for building your own graph-aware code analysis tools on top of the incremental knowledge graph.
